Sylvia De La Fuentes
Fresno, CA 93723 | The1stroundpick@gmail.com | 559-721-3608
 

Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Team,
When I think about Support and the importance of support while someone fights to transform their life in addiction and mental health care, I know firsthand that when someone reaches out for support, that first human connection can change everything. I thrive in those exact moments of uncertainty, bringing warmth, clarity, and genuine advocacy to help individuals take that brave first step toward recovery.

In my current role as Lead Program Aide at Beloved Survivors, I manage client intakes, assess support needs, and track service referrals to connect individuals with vital community resources. Whether I am guiding someone through housing options or navigating employment applications, my priority is always making sure no one falls through the cracks. I understand that intake is not just about processing information; it is about building instant trust, listening deeply to a person's barriers and motivations, and walking alongside them with unwavering empathy.

My background spans both compassionate healthcare support and fast-paced operational execution. At Aetna as a Medicare Customer Service Representative, I handled high-volume inbound calls and outbound follow-ups, verified eligibility details, and maintained strict HIPAA compliance while supporting members through complex coverage questions. Additionally, my experience managing Salesforce CRM datasets and high-volume workflows at Oriental Motor taught me how to move quickly across multiple live queues, stay organized in a technology-enabled environment, and treat metrics as tools to improve service quality rather than sources of pressure.

I bring a consultative, outcomes-driven mindset combined with a deep, personal commitment to expanding access to high-quality care. I am ready to bring my energy, heart, and organizational ownership to Adolescent Wellness Academy.
 
Warmly,
Sylvia De La Fuentes

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear AWA People & Culture team,

I first came across Adolescent Wellness Academy through a job post. With a bit of research, I found it to be a beloved program that changed many young lives for the better. As a creative professional with a growing interest in psychology and a wish to work with the younger crowd, I made a note to myself: Reach out. With my help as a social media professional, we can share your story, multiply the healing impact and foster deeper connections with the local community.

As a digital storyteller, I have spent the last decade sharpening my tools, working in all facets of content production from concept development to polished delivery with a brand-tailored, mission-aligned strategic foundation. At Little’s Photography, I worked closely with hundreds of high-schoolers as a fine-art senior portrait photographer and photo editor, while producing an extensive promotional video library for the studio’s marketing initiatives. Our promos reached thousands of clients and led to a surge in the sales of photoshoot packages. I produced organic social content for the Columbia College Chicago Student Communications IG feed, and filmed interview-based documentaries that were showcased all across the university campus. With consistent hard-work as a freelancer, one of my long-time remote clients Emel Onur now has 47,500+ followers on her YouTube channel, compared to the 50 followers we started our journey with.

More recently, I helped establish an Instagram account that is dear to me. My teenage cousin Kağan has a rare form of epilepsy called Dravet Syndrome. Against all odds, he joined the Turkish national tennis team in the special needs category. My aunt was inspired to share their story, so we can build a community and reach those who can help Kağan access the treatment he needs. In the last 3 months, our engagement surged and we got more than 200,000 views. More importantly, we connected with people in very meaningful ways and networked with a foundation who wants to conduct research to find the right treatment. It makes me very happy to be able to have a positive effect on my family and community in Turkey from thousands of miles away.

What excites me the most about the prospect of joining your team is that I wholeheartedly share the aspiration to provide a safe space for teens, where they feel loved and cared for, so we water the seeds of healing for generations to come. I’d appreciate the chance to discuss how I can contribute to your mission. You can reach me at 561-409-6908 or idilmeric@hotmail.com. Thank you for your time—I look forward to hearing from you.

Warm regards,
Idil Meric

questionnaire.text: What experience do you have supporting adolescents, families, or individuals receiving behavioral health services?
questionnaire.response:
In 1998 I worked for a year in the Department of Psychiatry assisting with HIV/AIDS patients. I sat in meetings and took notes as the Psychiatrist conducted group sessions with patients.. I ran to get tissues, water or just hold patients who were emotionally distressed and needed a shoulder.  Later in 2005, I moved to Florida and had my daughter. I waited for my son and daughter to be eligible for preK and kindergarten so I could return to work.   I found work as an ESOL paraprofessional helping High School students from other countries learn to speak English.  During those 9 years I learned not only to help many Spanish speaking students learn English, but how to care for the ones who were emotionally distressed from various personal problems at home, I would accompany them to the social workers office and translate all the problems they were experiencing at home. I realized how much suffering and empathy was needed for my role.  I later left the position to care for my son who had a massive brain tumor and barely survived during the surgery.  As my son, progressed and I was forced to stay home.  I found work on line, which happened to be during COVID. 
   I recently went back to work part time as a Substitute teacher, and still find myself helping students of all ages with a variety of emotional issues.

These qualities are not only essential in our personal lives at home with our families, but when dealing with all people, especially those battling illnesses and obstacles!

Celena Ditz, MS, LMFT
Kings Mountain, NC
(704) 418-2440 | celditz@gmail.com

October 26, 2026

Hiring Committee
Launch AWA NC
Re: Clinic Director – Adolescent Mental Health

Dear Hiring Committee,

I am writing to express my interest in the Clinic Director – Adolescent Mental Health position with Launch AWA NC. As a Licensed Marriage and Family Therapist with more than 25 years of experience in clinical and child-and-family services, including over 15 years in program and clinical leadership, I bring a combination of clinical expertise, operational management, staff development, and a strong commitment to improving outcomes for children, adolescents, and families. I am excited about the opportunity to apply my experience to a role focused on adolescent mental health and the delivery of high-quality, accessible clinical services.

In my current role as Director of Programs at Children’s Homes of Cleveland County/Core Family Services, I provide senior clinical and operational leadership across outpatient therapy, residential, independent living, and adoption programs. I also serve as Clinical Director of outpatient therapy, where I oversee clinical quality, clinician recruitment and supervision, service capacity, reimbursement, compliance, and ongoing program development. Throughout my tenure, I have worked to strengthen clinical services, support staff effectiveness, and ensure that programs meet the needs of the individuals and families they serve while maintaining appropriate clinical, contractual, and regulatory standards.

My experience has provided me with a strong understanding of the balance required to lead a successful behavioral health clinic. I have experience developing clinical capacity in response to community needs, supporting clinicians through supervision and consultation, managing after-hours clinical coverage for therapeutic emergencies, and collaborating with executive leadership on staffing, budgeting, and organizational planning. I believe effective clinical leadership requires both a commitment to sound clinical practice and the ability to build the systems, relationships, and processes that allow clinicians to provide meaningful, consistent care.

I also bring extensive experience in trauma-informed care, quality improvement, and clinical standards. As a Statewide Clinical Coach with Benchmarks NC Partnering for Excellence, I train, review, and evaluate trauma-intensive clinical assessments completed by clinicians across North Carolina, providing feedback and supporting consistency with established clinical standards. Additionally, I coordinate my agency’s performance and quality improvement and accreditation activities, including staff training, record reviews, corrective action planning, and continuous improvement initiatives. These experiences have strengthened my ability to evaluate clinical practices, identify opportunities for improvement, support professional development, and promote accountability while maintaining a focus on quality care.

In addition to my clinical background, I hold a Master of Science in Marriage and Family Therapy and a Master of Business Administration. This combination allows me to approach clinical leadership with an understanding of both the therapeutic needs of adolescents and families and the operational and financial considerations necessary to sustain and grow effective services. I value collaborative leadership, clear communication, thoughtful decision-making, and creating an environment where clinicians feel supported in their work and equipped to provide the highest quality of care.

Throughout my career, I have remained committed to serving children and families, particularly those impacted by trauma and other significant life challenges. I am particularly interested in the opportunity to contribute my experience to Launch AWA NC and help strengthen mental health services for adolescents. Given my extensive experience, clinical background, and leadership responsibilities, I would also welcome a conversation about compensation. I recognize that the position has a posted salary range; however, I am seeking compensation above that range that more fully reflects my qualifications and the value I would bring to the role. I hope there may be flexibility to discuss a package that aligns with my experience and the position’s responsibilities.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical background, leadership experience, and commitment to serving adolescents and families could contribute to the continued success of Launch AWA NC.

Sincerely,
Celena Ditz, MS, LMFT

work_history.title: Clinical Director
work_history.summary: Provide clinical leadership and oversight for behavioral health and substance use treatment services, supporting the delivery of safe, ethical, evidence-based, and recovery-oriented care. Provide clinical oversight and leadership for treatment services, ensuring clinical programming is implemented consistently and aligns with organizational, licensing, and accreditation requirements. Conduct comprehensive clinical assessments and determine appropriate ASAM level of care and treatment placement based on presenting needs, risk factors, withdrawal concerns, mental health symptoms, and recovery environment. Support clinical staff with diagnostic formulation, treatment planning, clinical interventions, documentation, and ongoing evaluation of client progress. Provide individual and group clinical supervision, case consultation, mentoring, and professional development to counselors and other assigned staff. Facilitate interdisciplinary treatment team meetings and clinical case consultations to promote coordinated, clinically appropriate care. Review clinical documentation and provide feedback regarding assessment quality, treatment plans, progress notes, group documentation, and continuity of care. Maintain a safe, structured, therapeutic environment and provide or coordinate crisis intervention and clinical response when indicated. Collaborate with medical, behavioral health, nursing, case management, and facility leadership teams to address complex client needs and promote continuity of care. Advocate for clients and incorporate client-centered perspectives into treatment planning, discharge planning, and recovery goals. Maintain accurate and timely clinical records and ensure completion of required documentation, training, and compliance activities.

I am excited to apply for the Bilingual Virtual Intake Coordinator position. With a Bachelor’s degree in Psychology, bilingual English–Spanish communication skills, and experience supporting clients remotely, I am prepared to help create a welcoming, organized, and compassionate first point of contact for adolescents and families seeking mental health services.

I am comfortable working independently, handling multiple tasks, maintaining accurate records, and communicating clearly across time zones. My background has strengthened my ability to listen actively, ask thoughtful questions, and respond calmly when individuals may be experiencing stress or uncertainty.

I also volunteer with Balakun, an organization dedicated to teaching English to teenagers in Ukraine. Through this role, I communicate virtually with young people, adapt to their individual needs, and provide consistent, encouraging support in a remote setting. This experience has strengthened my ability to build rapport with adolescents, remain patient and flexible, and create a positive, respectful environment for learning and communication.

My volunteer experience with El Refugio, a nonprofit supporting immigrant individuals and families affected by detention, further deepened my ability to provide compassionate, culturally sensitive support. I participated in visitation efforts and supported loved ones during difficult circumstances, which taught me the importance of dignity, confidentiality, patience, and clear communication. Combined with my psychology education, these experiences prepare me to support intake conversations with empathy while following organizational procedures and protecting client privacy.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my bilingual communication skills, organizational ability, and genuine commitment to adolescent well-being to your team. Thank you for considering my application. I would be glad to discuss how my experience can support your intake process and the families you serve.

Sincerely,
Sol Pomeroy

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Program Operations Manager – Adolescent Behavioral Health position. With over 20 years of experience in behavioral health, clinical services, program development, and organizational leadership, I bring a combination of clinical expertise and operational management experience that aligns well with the demands of overseeing behavioral health programs serving adolescents and their families.

Throughout my career, I have developed a strong foundation in program operations, staff supervision, quality improvement, regulatory compliance, and multidisciplinary collaboration. As the founder and Clinical Director of a behavioral health practice, I have directed clinical and administrative operations, developed policies and procedures, managed budgets and performance oversight, and led a multidisciplinary team of seven therapists and two administrative staff. My responsibilities have required balancing clinical quality, operational efficiency, ethical standards, and organizational growth while maintaining a strong commitment to individualized, trauma-informed care.

My experience also includes direct work with youth and vulnerable populations. As a Program Coordinator with Teen Living Programs, I supported children, youth, and young adults experiencing housing instability, coordinated community partnerships, supervised staff and interns, and contributed to program development and resource allocation. These responsibilities strengthened my understanding of the importance of structured, responsive programming, coordinated services, and organizational accountability when supporting young people navigating complex psychosocial challenges.

In addition, my clinical background includes working with individuals experiencing severe and persistent mental illness, trauma, substance use concerns, and other complex behavioral health needs. Through my work in Assertive Community Treatment and other clinical settings, I have developed expertise in crisis intervention, risk management, interdisciplinary coordination, and evidence-based treatment planning. I understand the importance of effective clinical oversight, clear operational protocols, staff development, and collaboration among providers to promote safety, continuity of care, and positive outcomes.

I would bring to this role a leadership approach that integrates clinical integrity with strategic and operational thinking. My strengths include developing effective programs, supporting and holding teams accountable, improving workflows, fostering collaborative partnerships, and ensuring that services remain responsive to the needs of the populations they serve. I am particularly interested in opportunities where I can apply my behavioral health leadership experience to strengthen adolescent services, support multidisciplinary teams, and contribute to programs that promote stability, resilience, and long-term well-being.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical background, program leadership, and operational experience could contribute to the continued success of your adolescent behavioral health services.

Sincerely,  
Romel Santiago, MSW, LCSW

questionnaire.text: If we asked this supervisor about your performance, what would they say was your most significant area for growth, and why?
questionnaire.response: As the owner and operator of a successful international private practice for over six years, I worked independently without a direct supervisor and was responsible for driving the vision, growth, and development of the business. During that time, I expanded services to include retreats, collaborations, and consulting with other practitioners and programs. One of my most significant areas of personal growth has been learning to balance professional ambition with self-care.  Because I was passionate about my work and continually identifying new opportunities for growth, I often found myself moving from one project or initiative to the next without taking sufficient time to pause, appreciate what I had accomplished, or recharge. While this drive contributed to the growth and success of the practice, it also taught me the importance of sustainability, boundaries, and intentional self-care.  This experience has helped me recognize that effective leadership is not simply about how much you can accomplish, but also about creating a sustainable pace that supports long-term effectiveness, sound decision-making, and personal well-being. I have learned the value of being more intentional about prioritizing, setting boundaries, and making space to reflect on accomplishments rather than constantly focusing on the next goal. I view this continued growth as an important part of becoming a more balanced and effective leader.

October 23, 2026 

Dear Hiring Committee, 

Thank you for taking the time to review my resume and cover letter. I am writing to express my enthusiasm for the opportunity to continue my experience working as a Registered Mental Health Counseling Intern at  Adolescent Wellness Academy. I received a Bachelor of Science in Psychology and am a recent graduate with my Masters in Mental Health Counseling from the University of Miami. 

As a motivated and compassionate clinician, I am interested in expanding my experience of working with evidence-based treatment modalities. 

My educational experiences have helped me to build my knowledge and experience for working as a registered mental health counseling intern. I have a strong academic background in psychology, as well as a strong interest in working with children and their families to address mental health challenges at an early age, including Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder, Anxiety, and Depression. Through my recent experiences working as a practicum intern at Nicklaus Children’s Hospital and the Institute for Individual and Family Counseling, I was able to establish a strong foundation in conceptualizing cases, applying interventions and building rapport. 

In my previous experience working at Florida International University’s Summer Treatment Program, I had the opportunity to work directly with children and their families, providing support in areas such as emotional regulation, coping skills, and behavioral management. These experiences have provided a good foundation in implementing therapeutic strategies tailored to the unique needs of young children, as well as solidified my interest in child and adolescent mental health. 

I have a passion for working with programs that help to provide low-cost services for a diverse population, as highlighted in my experience working as a practicum intern at the institute for Individual and Family Counseling. I believe that my strong communication skills and dedication will allow for a wonderful learning experience as I continue my work in the field of mental health counseling.  

I have included my resume and look forward to the possibility of discussing further my qualifications. Please feel welcome to contact me at your earliest convenience. I look forward to hearing from you. 

Respectfully, 
Morgan Reilly

Paula Lazarim, Ph.D., NCC

Hiring Committee
Adolescent Wellness Academy (AWA)
Boca Raton, Florida


Re: Primary Therapist Position

Dear Hiring Committee,

I am writing to express my interest in the Primary Therapist position at Adolescent Wellness Academy (AWA) in Boca Raton, Florida. With a Ph.D. in Counselor Education and Supervision, a master’s degree in Clinical Mental Health Counseling, and experience in clinical practice, counselor education, and clinical training, I bring an integrated perspective on mental health care that combines evidence-informed clinical approaches, developmental knowledge, multicultural awareness, and a commitment to supporting individuals through challenging life transitions. Having recently relocated back to Florida from Connecticut, I am currently working toward full licensure with the State of Florida and practicing as a Florida Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern (RMHCI). I am also legally authorized to live and work in the United States without employer sponsorship. I am particularly interested in AWA’s work with adolescents and its emphasis on individualized, collaborative care that supports emotional well-being, resilience, and personal growth, and I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to AWA’s work with adolescents and families from diverse backgrounds.

As a Portuguese-English bilingual professional with Spanish skills, I bring a multicultural perspective that supports my commitment to culturally responsive and accessible mental health care. My Brazilian background and international experience have shaped my appreciation for the ways culture, identity, family expectations, and transitions influence individuals’ experiences and help-seeking behaviors. I recognize the importance of building therapeutic relationships that honor clients’ culture and lived experiences while fostering trust, collaboration, and respect. 

My clinical experience and interests include working with concerns such as anxiety, depression, trauma, substance use/abuse, domestic violence, acculturation, relationship difficulties, and life transitions. My therapeutic approach reflects evidence-informed assimilative integration, grounded primarily in Narrative Therapy and Relational-Cultural Theory (RCT), while incorporating complementary approaches such as Solution-Focused Brief Therapy (SFBT), Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), and Motivational Interviewing (MI) to meet clients’ unique needs and therapeutic goals. I strive to create a warm, collaborative, and nonjudgmental therapeutic environment in which clients can explore their experiences, identify strengths, develop effective coping strategies, and work toward meaningful goals. My approach is grounded in cultural humility, trauma-responsive care, and an understanding of how relationships, family systems, cultural contexts, and broader social factors influence mental health and development.

I have a particular interest in human development across the lifespan, which is reflected in both my clinical work and my teaching. As an instructor, I have taught Lifespan and Human Development to counseling students, a course that deepens my engagement with developmental theories and how biological, psychological, social, cultural, and relational factors shape individuals’ experiences and well-being at different stages of life. This academic focus complements my interest in working with adolescents and understanding the unique developmental, emotional, interpersonal, and family-related challenges they may experience. I value developmentally responsive, trauma-informed, and strengths-based approaches that recognize each young person’s needs while engaging families and other members of the treatment team to support growth, resilience, and emotional well-being.

My clinical background also includes experience with individuals with autism and intellectual disabilities. In Brazil, I developed a project focused on social inclusion and group counseling for individuals with developmental disabilities, which gave me valuable experience understanding and addressing social, interpersonal, developmental, and emotional needs. This experience strengthened my commitment to adapting support to individuals’ unique circumstances and fostering environments that promote inclusion, connection, and personal growth. My background in career counseling further strengthened my experience supporting young individuals as they navigate transitions, develop self-awareness, and identify meaningful paths forward.

In addition to my clinical work, I served as an Assistant Professor of Practice and Clinical Training Director at Fairfield University in Connecticut, where I taught and mentored counseling students, coordinated clinical placements, collaborated with clinical supervisors and community partners, and supported students’ professional development. My responsibilities included coordinating field placements, communicating with supervisors and training sites, and helping students connect academic knowledge with clinical practice. This experience strengthened my ability to respectfully collaborate across professional roles, communicate effectively, maintain organized documentation, and appreciate the importance of coordinated care and professional accountability. My teaching experience in counseling skills, advanced treatment and counseling interventions, group work, ethics, career counseling, and human development also informs my understanding of therapeutic relationships, treatment planning, and the importance of adapting interventions to clients’ developmental and contextual needs.

I believe I am drawn to AWA’s multidisciplinary treatment environment and the opportunity to collaborate with therapists, psychiatrists, and other clinical professionals to support adolescents’ mental health and well-being. I value comprehensive, individualized treatment that integrates assessment, collaborative goal setting, therapeutic interventions, ongoing progress evaluation, family engagement, and continuity of care. I also recognize the importance of timely, accurate clinical documentation, ethical practice, appropriate consultation, and coordination with the treatment team to promote effective, consistent care.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical background, expertise in counselor education and human development, multicultural perspective, and commitment to accessible, trauma-responsive, strengths-based, and evidence-informed care could contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy and the adolescents and families it serves.

Sincerely,

Paula Lazarim, Ph.D., M.S., NCC
Florida Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear AWA Academy Team,

I am so excited to apply for the opportunity to join AWA Academy’s IOP/PHP team working with adolescents. As a therapist who graduated in December 2025, I am eager to continue growing as a clinician in a setting that aligns with something I am truly passionate about: supporting children, adolescents, and their families. I am especially drawn to AWA Academy because of the impact your work has on the lives of children and families, and I would love to be part of that mission.

I currently work as an intake therapist for a virtual IOP program, where I work with both adults and children. I also have experience working in an inpatient psychiatric hospital with adults, where I facilitated group therapy and conducted intake assessments. These experiences have helped me build my clinical skills, connect with clients from different backgrounds, and better understand the importance of compassionate, individualized care.

Before becoming a therapist, I worked as a special education teacher with children on the autism spectrum. Working with children and families was one of the most meaningful parts of my professional journey and played a big role in shaping the kind of therapist I wanted to become. I genuinely love working with kids and helping them feel understood, supported, and empowered. I would love the opportunity to bring that passion into my clinical work with adolescents and their families.

My therapeutic approach incorporates concepts from ACT and DBT, and I am excited to continue building on these skills while gaining more experience in individual therapy. I am eager to learn, grow, and challenge myself as a clinician, and I would be grateful for the opportunity to do so alongside a team that shares my commitment to supporting young people through difficult moments in their lives.

I am also fluent in both English and Portuguese, which allows me to connect with and support families from different linguistic and cultural backgrounds. I currently hold a license as a Registered Mental Health Intern and have a qualified supervisor. I anticipate to become fully licensed in a year and a half.

I would be genuinely excited to join AWA Academy and contribute to the meaningful work you do with children and families. Thank you for taking the time to consider my application. I would love the opportunity to connect and share more about my experience and enthusiasm for this role!

Thank you!

Rebecca Ubertini

To the Hiring Team at Adolescent Wellness Academy,
I am writing to express my strong interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position. Your mission to look past the drama and attitude to address the real underlying pain of struggling teenagers resonates deeply with me. Through my professional career in both high-volume remote contact centers and direct inpatient psychiatric care, I have built the exact dual skill set required to serve as a calm, compliant, and deeply empathetic first voice for families seeking a path to healing.
During my time at Rusk State Hospital, I worked directly with populations facing intense mental health challenges. Participating in interdisciplinary treatment team meetings provided me with profound clinical insight into co-occurring disorders. I listened to patients map out their histories, seeing directly how substance use frequently acted as a catalyst for severe, long-term psychiatric illnesses. This clinical backbone allows me to speak to parents and youth with genuine understanding, baseline authority, and extreme resilience during high-stakes crisis calls.
Complementing my clinical experience is a proven track record of remote, operational excellence. In my position with Conduent, I successfully orchestrated high-volume inbound phone pipelines while maintaining a 100% perfect Quality Assurance score for consecutive months. As a bilingual professional, I can also help Spanish-speaking individuals and families feel more comfortable communicating about treatment options and accessing support. I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position supporting Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. My professional background includes customer service, operational support, administrative documentation, and receptionist responsibilities. In my previous Operational Support role with HBCS, I reviewed documents for accuracy, reconciled payments and deposits, monitored assignments, and maintained documentation in accordance with company and regulatory requirements. I recognize that an admissions coordinator plays an important role in helping people take the first step toward treatment. I would approach each interaction with empathy and a commitment to helping callers understand the next steps in the admissions process. I am organized, dependable, detail-oriented, and committed to maintaining confidentiality and accurate records. I am also willing to learn the specialized systems and procedures required to support admissions workflows and protect sensitive client information.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my customer service experience, administrative strengths, and dedication to helping others to your team. Thank you for considering my application. I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. What especially interests me about this role is the opportunity to be the first supportive point of contact for individuals and families seeking mental-health or substance-use treatment. I understand that many of these conversations may happen during extremely difficult moments, and I would approach them with patience, empathy, professionalism, and respect. I am eager to learn the clinical and insurance-related aspects of the admissions process while bringing the communication and customer-care skills I have already developed.

I am currently pursuing my education while continuing to build a long-term career connected to psychology and mental health, making this opportunity especially meaningful to me. candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position specializing in adolescent mental health and substance use treatment. With an academic background in Psychology and Women’s and Gender Studies, along with hands-on experience working as a Behavioral Health Technician (BHT), I have developed a strong foundation in behavioral health, client support, and the importance of providing compassionate, individualized care to individuals and families.

Through my experience as a Behavioral Health Technician at Wishope Recovery, I gained valuable insight into the challenges individuals face when navigating mental health and substance use treatment. This experience strengthened my understanding of the importance of empathy, effective communication, confidentiality, and helping individuals access the support and resources they need. I understand that the admissions process can be an emotional and overwhelming experience for families, particularly when seeking treatment for an adolescent, and I would approach each interaction with professionalism, patience, and compassion.

My educational background in Psychology has helped me develop an understanding of human behavior, mental health, and the factors that influence an individual’s well-being. Additionally, my studies in Women’s and Gender Studies have strengthened my awareness of diversity, cultural differences, and the importance of providing inclusive, respectful care. I also bring leadership and organizational experience from coordinating a nursing home visitation program, where communication, responsibility, and relationship-building were essential to supporting others.

I am particularly interested in this position because it would allow me to combine my behavioral health experience and educational background with my passion for helping individuals and families navigate the treatment process. I recognize the importance of creating a positive first point of contact, gathering information accurately, communicating clearly with families and treatment teams, and helping connect adolescents with appropriate care. I am eager to contribute to a team that prioritizes mental health, recovery, and the well-being of young people.
Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience, education, and commitment to compassionate behavioral health services would make me a valuable addition to your team. I look forward to the possibility of contributing to your organization and helping adolescents and their families take meaningful steps toward recovery and improved well-being.
Sincerely,
Sierra Reyes

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager
I am writing to express my strong interest in the current position. With 18 years of dedication and leadership within the human services field, my passion for empowering vulnerable populations has been my driving force. My journey began when I transitioned from the corporate world, a decision that has provided me with immense personal and professional growth.
Throughout my career, I have worked across multiple specialized sectors—including developmental disabilities, mental health, substance use recovery, domestic violence, and housing instability—with a core focus on supporting children, families, and older adults within each system. As a Qualified Mental Health Professional (QMHP) and Qualified Intellectual Disabilities Professional (QIDP) who has completed the required substance abuse education, I am actively seeking an organization that provides approved supervision to fulfill Virginia Board of Counseling requirements for official CSAC Supervisee registration. I bring a strong clinical foundation and a versatile toolkit to conduct comprehensive assessments, implement evidence-based interventions, and deliver person-centered care across multidisciplinary settings.
I am deeply committed to being part of a team that makes a tangible difference in people's lives by providing support and guidance. I have learned that while anyone can become vulnerable, the right clinical and preventive services can build resilience and transform outcomes.
In my previous leadership roles, I honed my skills in fostering cross-functional collaboration and driving initiatives to improve both client service and team efficiency. I have a proven track record of building and leading high-performing teams, which includes taking the lead in interviewing and the hiring process, conducting employee evaluations, and supervising staff. My responsibilities have also included conducting internal audits and analyzing CQI reports, which directly led to improvements in accuracy and a reduction in operational redundancies. I consistently demonstrate excellent decision-making skills and understand the operational impact of those decisions, including managing call coverage and oversight.
My passion for this field is unwavering. I thrive on being part of a team that leads with empathy, understanding, and open-mindedness to continuous growth. I strongly believe that my clinical credentials, effective communication, organizational strengths, writing ability, interpersonal skills, and fluency in Spanish make me a distinct asset to your organization. As a leader, I am dedicated to not only engaging with clients directly but also providing individuals with reassurance, dignity, and a true sense of belonging—ensuring high-quality, accessible services that empower individuals to achieve maximum independence.
Thank you for your consideration. I have attached my resume for your review and welcome the opportunity to discuss how my qualifications, clinical credentials, and vision align with the needs of your team.
Respectfully,

work_history.title: Intake Counselor

Key Responsibilities: * Group Facilitation: Lead structured classes and therapeutic groups including Anger Management and Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), tailored to the correctional environment. * Intake Coordination: Serve as the intake specialist for clients entering treatment prior to release, ensuring accurate documentation and smooth transition into services. * Biopsychosocial Assessments: Conduct thorough assessments to identify psychological, social, and medical factors influencing substance use, forming the foundation for personalized master treatment plans. * Treatment Planning: Collaborate with clinical teams to design and implement recovery-oriented plans that align with each client's needs and goals. * Reentry Preparation: Support clients in preparing for successful reintegration by addressing relapse prevention, emotional regulation, and life skills.

work_history.title: Peer Supervisor Newborn substance exposure
work_history.summary: 1. One-on-One Peer Support & Facilitating Support Groups: * Building Trust: Start by creating a safe, non-judgmental space where individuals feel comfortable sharing their challenges and triumphs. Active listening is key here. * Facilitating Peer Groups: Lead group sessions where peers can share experiences, provide mutual support, and develop coping strategies. This could also include skill-building exercises, like communication techniques or stress management strategies. 1. Linking to Services & Resources: * Coordination: Help individuals identify and access services related to health, housing, employment, legal needs, etc. It's vital to know the available resources both inside and outside the facility. * Networking: Build relationships with service providers and maintain those connections so you can quickly connect clients with necessary resources. 1. Advocacy & Empowerment: * Advocating for Rights: Be an advocate for clients' rights, ensuring they have access to needed services, fair treatment, and that their preferences are respected. * Self-Advocacy Skills: Teach clients how to advocate for themselves in different settings, which is an essential part of recovery and independence. 1. Support in Day-to-Day Life: * Modeling Behaviors: Demonstrate positive behaviors and coping mechanisms. This could involve showing healthy ways to manage stress, navigate conflict, or practice mindfulness. * Life Skills Development: Focus on skills like budgeting, cooking, time management, and goal-setting. These practical tools help clients develop independence and confidence. 1. Counseling & Guidance: * Providing Counseling: Offer emotional and psychological support, especially as clients work through difficult issues like addiction, trauma, and adjusting to life in or after incarceration. * Mentoring: Offer guidance on setting realistic goals and following through with them, from sobriety to employment and personal growth. 1. Documentation & Reporting: * Accurate Documentation: Ensure all activities, interactions, and progress are recorded according to the program's guidelines. This is crucial for maintaining continuity of care and for reporting purposes. 1. Community & Social Engagement: * Organizing Events: Coordinate social activities, outings, or group projects that encourage social interaction and community building, which is essential for rehabilitation and reintegration. * Promoting Wellness: Lead initiatives that focus on physical and mental well-being, such as fitness routines, nutritional guidance, or stress-relief practices. Key Skills for Success: Cultural Competence: Understanding the diverse backgrounds and needs of incarcerated individuals, ensuring that services are tailored and sensitive to their unique experiences. * Patience & Resilience: Working in this field often involves setbacks, but remaining patient and adaptable is crucial for success. * Teamwork & Collaboration: While you're supporting individuals, you'll also need to work closely with other service providers, families, and team members to ensure a cohesive support system. * Crisis Management: Being prepared to handle crises (whether emotional, health-related, or social) in a calm and effective manner.

work_history.title: Peer Recovery Specialist/case Manager
work_history.summary: * Visiting Pregnant Patients with Substance Use Disorder: * Building Trust: One of the first steps when visiting these patients is to establish trust. Substance use disorder, particularly during pregnancy, can often carry feelings of shame or fear of judgment. Creating an environment of empathy and non-judgmental support is crucial. * Physical and Emotional Support: You likely provided both emotional support to help them cope with recovery and practical advice to support their physical well-being during pregnancy. This can involve counseling, stress reduction techniques, and offering tools to help manage cravings or urges. * Assisting During Recovery to Prevent Relapse: * Prevention Focus: Preventing relapse is critical to ensuring the health of both the mother and the fetus. This involves continuous monitoring, encouragement, and working with the patient on coping strategies to manage triggers or stressful situations that may lead to relapse. * Education: Educating the patient about the potential consequences of substance use during pregnancy and how it could affect fetal development. This knowledge can help increase their motivation to stay clean. * Referrals for Psychological Therapy and Medication Treatment: * Coordinating Care: Ensuring that these patients are not only supported during their visits but are also connected to a comprehensive treatment plan involving therapy and medical support. This could involve finding a therapist specializing in substance use or working with a doctor to provide medication-assisted treatment (MAT) that's safe during pregnancy. * Holistic Approach: The combination of psychological therapy and medical treatment is key in addressing both the emotional and physical aspects of substance use disorder. Collaborating with both mental health professionals and physicians is important to provide holistic care. * Collaboration in Program Development: * Creating a New Initiative: Since this program was new to Citrus County, your role in developing and implementing it shows your leadership and initiative. This likely involved working with other healthcare professionals, stakeholders, and perhaps community leaders to ensure that the program would be both effective and sustainable. * Program Design: In collaboration with others, you may have had to design protocols for patient care, outline treatment options, and set up follow-up procedures to track patient progress. This could have involved crafting educational materials or creating resource networks for patients in recovery. * Community Awareness: A new program also often requires outreach and education within the community to ensure that both potential patients and healthcare providers are aware of the resources available. * Ongoing Evaluation and Adjustments: * Data and Feedback Collection: For new programs, it's essential to monitor and evaluate how well the intervention is working. This could involve collecting feedback from patients, healthcare providers, and community partners, as well as analyzing outcomes. * Making Adjustments: Based on the initial phase of the program, you may have been involved in making adjustments to the program's structure, referral processes, or treatment options to better meet the needs of the community.

With over five years of experience in behavioral health admissions and a broader background in mental health, substance use disorder treatment, and crisis support, I bring a strong understanding of the admissions process and the importance of connecting individuals with the appropriate level of care.

Throughout my career, I have worked directly with individuals and families seeking treatment during some of the most challenging moments of their lives. My experience includes handling incoming admissions inquiries, conducting initial screenings, gathering relevant information, verifying insurance benefits, coordinating with clinical and admissions teams, and helping prospective clients navigate the process of entering treatment. I understand the importance of responding promptly, communicating compassionately, maintaining confidentiality, and balancing the needs of prospective patients with the operational requirements of a treatment program.

I recognize that the admissions process is often a critical first step toward recovery. I strive to make every interaction professional, supportive, and informative while helping individuals and families feel heard and understood. I am comfortable managing competing priorities, handling sensitive conversations, and working in fast-paced environments where attention to detail, sound judgment, and follow-through are essential.

I am particularly interested in a remote opportunity where I can apply my behavioral health experience, strong communication skills, and commitment to helping people access treatment. I am dependable, adaptable, and comfortable working independently while collaborating with a team to meet organizational goals and provide a positive experience for those seeking care.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience and dedication to behavioral health admissions could contribute to your organization and the individuals you serve.

Sincerely,
Holly Brim

candidates.cover_letter:
My academic background in psychology and my professional experience supporting individuals and families have shaped my commitment to helping people access the resources and support they need to thrive. I was particularly drawn to Adolescent Wellness Academy’s philosophy of treating people, not symptoms, and its commitment to creating a safe, supportive, and nonjudgmental environment where adolescents and their families can heal and grow together. I believe that helping someone access care begins with making them feel heard, respected, and supported. I would be excited to contribute to this mission as a Virtual Admissions Coordinator by helping adolescents and families navigate the admissions process with compassion, clarity, and understanding.

I earned my Bachelor of Arts from Widener University, where I studied Psychology and Gender and Women’s Studies and minored in International Relations. My academic background provided me with a foundation in human behavior, interpersonal relationships, and the importance of understanding individuals within their broader social and family contexts. Through my academic and professional experiences, I have developed an appreciation for person-centered approaches that recognize each individual's unique circumstances, strengths, and challenges. I would bring this perspective to interactions with families who may be navigating uncertainty or seeking mental health support for their adolescents.

In my current role as an Employment Specialist at DiscoverAbility, I work directly with individuals to identify opportunities that align with their goals, strengths, and needs. I guide participants through the employment process by assisting with applications, developing resumes and cover letters, identifying appropriate opportunities, and maintaining accurate documentation of their progress. This role has strengthened my ability to build rapport, communicate information clearly, provide individualized guidance, and manage responsibilities with attention to detail. Previously, as an intern with Elwyn’s Early Learning Services, I gained experience supporting young children with developmental delays and disabilities and their families. I contributed to efforts focused on promoting child development, strengthening family capacity, and helping families access the support they needed. These experiences reinforced the importance of patience, empathy, and collaboration when working with individuals and families navigating unfamiliar or challenging circumstances.

My experience with Maryland Hunger Solutions further strengthened my ability to connect individuals with essential resources. Through outreach and advocacy initiatives, I collaborated with community partners and assisted individuals in accessing programs such as SNAP, local food banks, and school meal services. I also helped develop communication materials, including Spanish-language resources, to improve accessibility for Spanish-speaking communities. This experience taught me that connecting people with services requires more than providing information; it requires listening to their concerns, explaining available resources in accessible language, and helping them understand their next steps. As someone fluent in both English and Spanish, I would bring this same commitment to culturally responsive communication when interacting with adolescents, parents, and referral partners.

What stands out to me about Adolescent Wellness Academy is its recognition that supporting adolescents also means supporting their families. Seeking mental health treatment can be an overwhelming process for parents and teens alike, and the first interaction with an admissions team can help establish a sense of trust and reassurance. I would approach these conversations with compassion, professionalism, and respect, recognizing the importance of helping each family feel heard while guiding them toward appropriate next steps. I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my communication, organizational, and client-support skills to an admissions process that reflects AWA’s commitment to individualized care, family involvement, and lasting growth.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my background in psychology, experience supporting individuals and families, and commitment to accessible, person-centered services could contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy’s mission.

October 21, 2026

Re: Virtual Admissions Coordinators
Dear Hiring Team,
I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position at AWA. Your mission to help not only the youth you serve, but the family as a whole is a strong match for the work I have done throughout my career.
For more than ten years, I have worked in roles where accuracy and confidentiality were not optional. As a Program Manager at Community Violence Solutions, I audited 100–200 client records every month in an Excel-based database, maintaining 100% accuracy and strict confidentiality. I managed high-volume documentation workflows against firm compliance deadlines, cross-checked data across multiple platforms, and produced reports for county, state, and federal funders. I also supervised a team of five to seven employees and trained them on data entry and documentation, so I know how to keep detail-oriented work consistent across a team. The work that I completed was all done with love and care for the family unit. We thrived in helping youth and families throughout their healing process. 
Earlier in my career, I managed active caseloads of 30 to 50+ clients at a time, completing intakes, case data entry, and monthly documentation for each one. I also provided customer and tech support in person and by chat as a part-time Customer Support Specialist at Sprint, handling setups, activations, and troubleshooting. Answering calls, working with limited supervision, and adjusting to changing priorities are things I do every day. I work comfortably in Word, Excel, Outlook, Google Workspace, Zoom, and Teams, and I have spent several years working fully remotely.
What I would bring to AWA most of all is a deep respect for the people behind the records. I have spent my career helping people in difficult moments, and I understand how important it is that sensitive information reaches only the right hands. I am eager to build on that foundation by learning HIPAA regulations and AWA,s procedures, and by developing into a dependable, high-quality member of your team. As a fully bilingual English and Spanish speaker, I also communicate clearly and professionally with a wide range of customers.
Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience can support your team, and I can be reached at 415-948-3875 or lray1214@gmail.com.

Sincerely,

Lucia Ray-Guillen

Inez D. Kearse
Covington, GA
470-301-4009 | inezdenice@gmail.com

October 21, 2026

Dear Hiring Team,

I believe the person answering that first phone call can make all the difference in whether someone takes the next step toward getting help. That is what caught my attention about this opportunity. You're not simply looking for someone to answer calls and schedule appointments. You're looking for someone who can recognize the importance of that moment, connect with the person on the other end of the phone, and help them move forward. That is exactly the kind of work I enjoy doing.

I bring a combination of remote admissions experience, behavioral health support, and genuine compassion for people who are navigating difficult circumstances. During my time with Ultimate Medical Academy, I worked remotely in admissions, interviewing prospective students, managing a high volume of inquiries, maintaining CRM records, and following up with individuals throughout the enrollment process. I ranked number one in my division and achieved 380% of my enrollment target. Those results came from more than meeting performance expectations. I understood how to build relationships, listen to people's needs, address their concerns, and remain consistent in my follow-through.

What makes my background especially relevant is that I also understand the importance of emotional support. Through my work with Youth Villages and my experience in family support counseling, I've worked with individuals and families facing behavioral challenges, emotional difficulties, and circumstances that require patience, compassion, and sound judgment. I've learned that people do not always know how to communicate what they need, especially when they're overwhelmed. Sometimes you have to listen beyond the initial question to understand how you can actually help.

I recognize that behavioral health admissions are different from educational admissions. Families seeking mental health or substance use treatment may be frightened, exhausted, or uncertain about what happens next. I would approach those conversations with the same care I would want someone to show my own family, while ensuring that inquiries, documentation, referrals, and follow-ups are handled professionally and accurately.

I'm comfortable working independently in a remote environment, managing multiple conversations and responsibilities, maintaining confidential information, and following through until the next step is clear. I would welcome the opportunity to learn your admissions processes and become a dependable part of the team supporting Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center.

I am confident in what I bring to this position, but what matters most to me is the opportunity to use my experience in a way that genuinely impacts someone's life. I would love the opportunity to speak with you about how I can contribute to your admissions team.

Thank you for your time and consideration.

Sincerely,
Inez D. Kearse

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. As a Certified Peer Recovery Specialist with national certification and hands-on experience in behavioral health admissions, intake coordination, insurance verification, and Kipu EMR, I bring a strong combination of operational knowledge, clinical understanding, and compassionate communication to this opportunity.

Throughout my career in behavioral health and substance use treatment, I have supported individuals and families during some of their most challenging and vulnerable moments. My professional experience includes managing intake inquiries, assisting with admissions processes, verifying insurance benefits, coordinating treatment referrals, maintaining accurate electronic health records, and helping individuals navigate appropriate levels of care. I am familiar with PHP and IOP treatment settings and understand the importance of timely communication, accurate documentation, and a seamless admissions experience.

My hands-on experience with Kipu EMR has strengthened my ability to manage patient information, maintain organized records, and support efficient clinical and administrative workflows. Additionally, my background providing remote behavioral health services has equipped me with the independence, adaptability, and attention to detail necessary to succeed in a fast-paced virtual admissions environment.

Beyond my technical qualifications, I bring a genuine passion for connecting individuals with life-changing treatment. Through my training in Motivational Interviewing, Wellness Recovery Action Planning (WRAP), Mental Health First Aid for Youth and Adults, trauma informed care, and overdose prevention, I have developed the ability to establish trust, navigate sensitive conversations, and support individuals experiencing mental health and substance use challenges.

I understand that for many adolescents and families, the admissions process represents their first step toward healing. I take pride in ensuring that every interaction is handled with professionalism, empathy, urgency, and respect. My goal is always to help individuals feel supported while making the process of accessing treatment as clear and manageable as possible.

I am particularly drawn to this opportunity because it allows me to combine my admissions experience, technical proficiency, and commitment to behavioral health advocacy in a meaningful remote role. I am confident that my familiarity with Kipu, insurance verification, treatment coordination, and patient engagement would allow me to contribute positively to your admissions team from day one.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience, qualifications, and dedication to helping individuals access quality behavioral health treatment align with the mission of Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center.

Sincerely,

Jennifer Gribble
CPRS, NCPRSS

Virtual Admissions Coordinator
Adolescent Mental Health & Substance Use Treatment
October 20, 2026
Hiring Team
Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center
Dear Hiring Team,
When a parent calls about a struggling teenager, or an adult finally reaches out about their substance use, the first voice they hear matters. I have spent more than 20 years being that voice, and I would love to bring that experience to Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center as a Virtual Admissions Coordinator.
My career has been built on admissions, assessment, and referral work. At National Healthcare Associates, I handled inbound referrals from several hospital systems at once for multiple facilities, screened each client against admission criteria, and decided whether to accept, deny, or refer them elsewhere. I verified benefits, secured Medicare, Medicaid, and commercial authorizations, and advocated directly with insurers to keep admissions from stalling. Before that, I spent 17 years as Regional Clinical Admissions Director for Kindred Healthcare, managing the full referral to admission cycle for adults with psychiatric and behavioral needs, including co-occurring drug and alcohol use disorders.
I am used to owning my pipeline without daily direction. At Kindred I independently ran a four-state territory, building relationships with case managers, social workers, and discharge planners both virtually and in person, and following up consistently until every referral had a clear outcome. That work generated enough admissions that the organization opened additional units and a new facility. I am comfortable working in CRM and EMR systems, including EPIC, Navi, and Allscripts, and I keep accurate, HIPAA-compliant records.
I also bring a counselor's foundation. I hold an M.S. in Mental Health Counseling and an M.S.Ed. in School Counseling from Syracuse University, my early clinical work included adolescents in day treatment and residential programs, and I served as board president of YouthHarbor. As a Reiki Master Teacher and owner of Beehive Wellness, I meet people in difficult moments with calm and compassion, which is exactly how I would greet your callers.
I would welcome the chance to talk about how I can help families and adults move from that first call to a clear next step. Thank you for your time and consideration.
Sincerely,
Keli Scott

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the **Virtual Admissions Coordinator: Adolescent Mental Health & Substance Use Treatment** position. With my  experience supporting individuals with behavioral health needs and mental illness, I am confident that my clinical support skills, compassion, communication abilities, and dedication to patient care would make me a valuable addition to your team.

In my previous role at a 140-bed private psychiatric hospital, I provided care and support to adult patients ranging from geriatric individuals to returning veterans. Working under the direction of nursing and medical staff, I helped patients adjust to new routines, participate in social and therapeutic activities, and complete daily living tasks. I monitored patient behavior, maintained appropriate boundaries, assessed safety concerns, and responded effectively to crisis situations, including assisting with restraints when necessary to prevent injury.

In addition to my direct patient-care experience, I have developed strong skills in behavioral health referrals, admissions, and intake coordination. I am comfortable answering inbound calls and responding to inquiries from clients, parents and guardians, families, referral sources, and healthcare providers. I communicate with patience, empathy, and professionalism while gathering essential information, identifying immediate concerns, and helping families understand available treatment options.

I am familiar with explaining Partial Hospitalization Programs (PHP) and Intensive Outpatient Programs (IOP) in clear, caring, and easy-to-understand language. I understand that families seeking adolescent mental health or substance use treatment may be experiencing significant stress, and I approach each interaction with sensitivity, respect, and a nonjudgmental attitude. I can help families understand program expectations, levels of care, next steps, and the admissions process while ensuring that urgent safety concerns are communicated promptly to the appropriate clinical staff.

My additional qualifications include:

- Answering inbound calls and responding professionally to inquiries from adolescents, parents, guardians, families, providers, and referral sources  
- Gathering accurate demographic, clinical, insurance, and referral information during initial conversations  
- Screening prospective clients for program fit based on presenting concerns, treatment needs, age, safety considerations, and level of care  
- Explaining PHP, IOP, mental health, and substance use treatment services in a clear and compassionate manner  
- Recognizing potential safety concerns and escalating urgent situations according to established protocols  
- Verifying insurance eligibility and benefits and assisting with authorization-related information  
- Coordinating clinical assessments, intake appointments, admission dates, and required paperwork  
- Communicating with families, providers, clinicians, and other members of the treatment team to support a smooth admissions process  
- Following up consistently with every caller until the individual is scheduled, connected with services, or appropriately referred elsewhere  
- Maintaining accurate and timely documentation in CRM and electronic medical record systems  
- Entering referral and admissions information accurately while protecting confidential patient information  
- Completing documentation in accordance with HIPAA requirements and organizational policies  
- Tracking referrals, follow-up activity, scheduling status, and outcomes to ensure that no inquiry is overlooked  
- Remaining organized, responsive, and professional while managing multiple calls, referrals, and admissions tasks  
- Monitoring patient safety, behavior, vital signs, and overall condition in a psychiatric hospital setting  
- Supporting patients with personal care, daily activities, socialization, and rehabilitation  
- Remaining calm and effective during high-stress conversations and crisis situations  

I am passionate about helping adolescents and families connect with the appropriate behavioral health and substance use treatment services. My combination of hands-on psychiatric experience, referral coordination, insurance verification, admissions support, documentation, and strong interpersonal skills would allow me to contribute effectively to your virtual admissions team.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience and qualifications align with the needs of your organization. I look forward to hearing from you.

Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

Howdy! I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy because this role reflects the kind of work I have spent years doing: showing up for people when they are struggling, building trust when trust does not come easily, and helping individuals feel supported without judgment.
I bring more than seven years of direct behavioral health experience working with children, adolescents, adults, and older adults facing complex mental health, behavioral, and co-occurring substance use challenges. At Promises Behavioral Health, I supported adults ages 18 to 81 in residential and partial hospitalization settings. My work required constant observation, strong boundaries, de-escalation, crisis response, accurate documentation working with Kipu, teamwork with clinicians, and—perhaps most importantly—the ability to connect with people who were overwhelmed, guarded, resistant, or simply having a very difficult day.
Before that, at Halifax Behavioral Health, I worked with at-risk children and adolescents ages 4 to 17. That experience taught me how much can be communicated without words and how important consistency, patience, calmness, and genuine human connection are when someone does not yet feel safe enough to engage.
Those same lessons have followed me throughout nearly three decades of equine work. Through my current business, Healed By The Horse, I create individualized experiences centered on trust, emotional awareness, regulation, confidence, and connection. Horses have reinforced something I already knew from behavioral health: you cannot force trust. You earn it by being present, observant, consistent, and authentic.
That is what draws me to remote work with Adolescent Wellness Academy.
I understand that meaningful mental health is not achieved by treating a diagnosis while overlooking the person living with it. People need to know that someone sees them, hears them, respects their experience, and will continue showing up. I would bring that mindset—along with substantial hands-on behavioral health experience, strong observational skills, compassion, professional boundaries, and a steady presence—to the Virtual Admissions Coordinator role.
I am also comfortable working independently, communicating virtually, documenting electronically via Kipu, learning new systems, and collaborating closely with multidisciplinary care teams. The opportunity to provide meaningful support within a virtual treatment environment is especially appealing to me.
I would be proud to bring my experience, patience, intuition, and very genuine commitment to helping people to Adolescent Wellness Academy. 

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to speak with you about how I could contribute to your team and, most importantly, to the individuals you serve.

Warmly,

Kris Secor

I am excited to apply for the Adolescent Services Manager position. My background in
education and student services has given me extensive experience leading teams,
coordinating day-to-day operations, managing competing priorities, and creating
structured environments where young people can feel supported and successful. I am
especially drawn to this role because it combines the organization and problem-solving I
enjoy with the opportunity to make a meaningful difference in the experience of
adolescents and their families.

staff and students, managing schedules and logistics, maintaining accurate records, and
making sure day-to-day operations stay on track. In my previous roles, I have worked
with multidisciplinary teams, coordinated services and resources, addressed concerns
as they arose, and communicated with a wide range of stakeholders. I am comfortable
stepping in when something isn't working, figuring out what needs to be done, and
creating a practical solution.

expectations, reliable routines, strong communication, and a supportive environment can
make a significant difference. I would bring a calm, organized approach to supervising

available to support the team when challenges arise.

My experience has also required me to balance many details at once, including

unexpected issues. I am someone who naturally looks ahead, notices what needs
attention, and takes pride in keeping things organized. I believe those strengths would
translate well to managing program flow, staff coverage, attendance, intake coordination,
safety procedures, and the administrative responsibilities of this position.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, organization, and problem-

adolescents and families feel safe, respected, and supported.

Thank you for your consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to speak with you
about how my background could contribute to your team.

Sincerely,

Melanie Negron
